title: Three consecutive factors
statement: Prove that (n + 9)(n + 10)(n + 11) is divisible by 6 for every integer n.
solution: Among three consecutive integers one is divisible by 3. At least one is even, so the product is divisible by 2 as well. Since gcd(2,3)=1, their product 6 divides the product. This reasoning includes zero and negative factors.

title: An invariant greatest common divisor
statement: Prove that gcd(n, n + 10) = gcd(n, 10) for every positive integer n.
solution: If d divides both n and n+10, it divides their difference 10; hence d is a common divisor of n and 10. Conversely, if d divides n and 10, it divides n+10. The sets of positive common divisors coincide, so their greatest members coincide.
